paper_title: An analysis of vaccine-related sentiments from development to deployment   of COVID-19 vaccines
caption: : Polarity scores for Japan
model_annotation: The plot illustrates the distribution of tweet (or text) counts across polarity score bins for Japan by showing how the number of observations varies with polarity score. The x-axis is labeled “Polarity scores,” uses a linear scale, and spans roughly from −1.1 to 0.6 with regularly spaced tick labels at about 0.2 intervals (−1.0, −0.8, −0.6, −0.4, −0.2, 0.0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6). The y-axis is labeled “Counts,” uses a linear scale, and ranges from 0 up to a little over 40,000 with major ticks at 0, 10,000, 20,000, 30,000, and 40,000. A single blue solid line with circular markers is shown; it starts near 0 counts at the most negative polarity scores (around −1.1 to −0.9), rises to a few hundred by about −0.8, reaches several thousand by around −0.5 (about 5,000), dips to a few thousand around −0.4 to −0.35, then increases through approximately 8,000 at about −0.25 and roughly 13,000 at about −0.2, climbs to around 27,000 near −0.1, and peaks at approximately 42,000 at 0.0. After 0.0, the line drops to roughly 8,500 near 0.1, rises again to about 26,000 around 0.2, falls to around 9,000 near 0.3 and to under 1,000 near 0.4, increases again to roughly 13,000 near 0.5, and ends near a few hundred by about 0.55.
